fields.title: Planned absences
fields.what: Working days on which a person is not available for sprint work: vacation, time off, training, conferences, other projects. Do NOT enter public holidays – they are taken into account automatically via the German state.
fields.source: Vacation calendar or asking the team. Half days as 0.5.
fields.example: 2 days of vacation + half a day of training → 2.5

fields.title: Absence status
fields.what: Each sprint has one of three states: “unknown” (nothing recorded: the capacity comes from calendar and people list, absences are estimated from the last sprints), “announced” (absences entered but not yet confirmed) and “confirmed” (absences confirmed, or explicitly “nobody is absent”). Without an explicit confirmation a sprint is never “confirmed”.
fields.example: Sprint 2026.23: no entries, “Nobody is absent” ticked → confirmed, full staffing

fields.title: FTE and workweek
fields.what: FTE is the share of a person's working days that they work in the team (1 = all their working days). The workweek (e.g. mon,tue,wed,thu) defines which weekdays are their working days. Please model part-time only once: either the full workweek with FTE 0.8 or the four-day week with FTE 1 – not both, otherwise it is deducted twice (10 days → 8 × 0.8 = 6.4 instead of 8 PT).
fields.source: Employment contract or agreement with the person (People page).
fields.example: 10 working days in the sprint: Mon–Fri + FTE 0.8 → 8 PT · mon,tue,wed,thu + FTE 1 → 8 PT · Mon–Fri + FTE 0.5 (half time) → 5 PT

fields.title: Deduction for Scrum events
fields.what: Time for dailies, planning, review, retro and refinement that is not available for tickets. Either in percent or as fixed PT per person and sprint (× FTE) – both are the same deduction in two units, the fields synchronize. If PT per person are set, they apply instead of the percentage. The deduction works the same for confirmed, expected and estimated absences: first holidays and absences, then the deduction. Rounding only happens when shown and when frozen.
fields.example: 1 PT per person with 10 working days equals 10 %; full time: −1 PT, half time (FTE 0.5): −0.5 PT

fields.title: Capacity
fields.what: Available person days (PT) of the team in the sprint. Normally calculated from the people list, holidays and absences and frozen at the review.
fields.source: Automatic. Only enter manually if there is no people list.

fields.title: Commitment
fields.what: The amount committed in sprint planning for THIS sprint: the sum of the estimates of all tickets in the sprint at sprint start. Not the velocity of the previous sprint; tickets added later count as scope creep.
fields.source: Right after planning: sum of the estimates on the board, or in Jira the value "Commitment" in the sprint report/velocity chart. Equals carry-over + backlog; if left empty it is prefilled with this sum from the cross-check.

fields.title: Velocity
fields.what: Amount actually done in the sprint: estimates of the finished tickets plus – by team practice – the parts of open tickets completed in the sprint (estimate of the ticket, not the actual effort). See “Done per product”.
fields.source: At the review: sprint report, or in Jira the value "Completed" in the velocity chart.

fields.title: Scope creep
fields.what: Share of work added to the sprint after planning, relative to the commitment (0.3 = 30 %). Leave empty if unknown – do not enter 0.
fields.source: Sprint report: estimates added later / commitment.

fields.title: Carry-over (remaining effort)
fields.what: Remaining effort of unfinished tickets taken over from the previous sprint. Part of the optional cross-check – only affects the planning delta.

fields.title: Backlog
fields.what: Sum of the tickets newly planned in the planning. Part of the optional cross-check; carry-over + backlog equals the commitment.

fields.title: Correction of remaining effort
fields.what: Parts of tickets already done that are still included in the planning value (subtracted). Separate several values with spaces. Part of the optional cross-check – only affects the planning delta.

fields.title: PO pre-planning per product
fields.what: Amount the PO of a product intends for the sprint – before planning, as a basis for agreement between the POs. Compared with the standard (available amount / number of products handled).
fields.source: PO meeting or the POs' preparation, e.g. sum of the intended tickets.

fields.title: Planning per product
fields.what: Amount planned for the product in sprint planning (sum of the product's tickets in the sprint).
fields.source: Sprint board at planning, filtered by product (component, label, epic …).

fields.title: Done per product
fields.what: Amount actually done for the product in the sprint: estimates of the finished tickets plus the parts of open tickets completed in the sprint (team practice). The sum over the products is at most the velocity. This way of counting should be uniform in the team – otherwise velocity and done are not comparable between teams or across a change.
fields.source: At the review: sprint report, filtered by product.

workflow.title: Set up the team
workflow.text: Create a new team, then add the people with their FTE share.

workflow.title: Create future sprints
workflow.text: Following sprints are created automatically from the sprint length and the end of the previous one. In the sprint calendar they can be created in advance, and different lengths (e.g. over Christmas) set via the last day; the following sprints shift accordingly. The capacity counts the working days of the sprint, so the Forecast PLAN scales with the length. Enter bridge days as absences.

workflow.title: Maintain absences
workflow.text: As soon as vacations, training etc. are known, enter them per person and sprint – also for future sprints. If none are known, explicitly confirm “Nobody is absent”. Without confirmation the absences stay “unknown” and are estimated from the last sprints.

workflow.title: View the forecast
workflow.text: Shows the Forecast PLAN for the current and upcoming sprints – the recommended planning amount, split into plannable and small items. The Today page shows what is due next.

workflow.title: PO pre-planning per product
workflow.text: Only with product distribution switched on (settings). If the team looks after several products, the POs enter how much they plan per product – compared to the default (available amount / number of products).

workflow.title: Planning in three steps
workflow.text: 1. Confirm the absences of the sprint (Prepare). 2. Plan the tickets with the Forecast PLAN, optionally per product. 3. Before the sprint starts, enter the commitment (the amount committed) and freeze the plan; the Forecast PLAN is frozen at that point. Optionally the cross-check from carry-over, backlog and corrections (delta to the Forecast PLAN).

workflow.title: Record the review
workflow.text: Enter velocity, scope creep and optionally done per product. The sprint's capacity is frozen so that later changes to the people list do not change the history. Product values are entered only on the boards (pre-planning, planning, review); the product distribution only evaluates them.

workflow.title: Analysis
workflow.text: In addition to the forecast: range (conservative/optimistic), focus factor, buffer recommendation and "When will it be done?" for a remaining amount.

workflow.title: People and settings
workflow.text: Record joining, leaving and FTE changes; adjust team settings such as German state or reference capacity.
workflow.cli: foresprint people TEAM · foresprint settings TEAM

workflow.title: Maintain products
workflow.text: Only with product distribution switched on. Create new products (with PO if “PO assignment” is on) and start date; end handed-over ones with “until” instead of deleting – past reports are kept.

terms: Available person days in the sprint (always PT, also for SP teams).
The amount committed at planning – the commitment at sprint start, not a result (formerly “Forecast IST”; the file keys are still called forecast_ist).

Velocity / capacity × reference capacity. Makes sprints with vacation and fully staffed sprints comparable. The same quantity as the focus factor, just scaled by the reference capacity; the reference capacity does not change the Forecast PLAN.
Velocity / capacity (= normalized velocity / reference capacity). Not comparable between teams because it depends on the estimation unit; the trend within one's own team is what counts.
Average of the last sprints with a value (default 5, adjustable). Sprints without a value do not count; the window then reaches further back.
Extrapolation of the average into the future. Default “constant” (last average). “Linear” and “classic” also extrapolate noise and must be chosen explicitly; with thin history “constant” applies.

Example: the average was 44 recently, 40 before. Constant (default): the next sprints stay at 44, 44, 44. Robust, but follows no development. Linear: the last step (+4) continues: 48, 52, 56. Classic: linear first (48), then proportional like the last time (+10 %: 52.8), then linear again (57.6). Linear and classic also extrapolate random fluctuations; the forecast can then rise or fall strongly over a longer horizon. They only fit a proven, stable trend. If the history is not enough (fewer sprints with a value than the mode needs), “constant” applies, and a note says so. The forecast is never negative. You can switch the mode at any time under Manage team → Settings; no data is lost, the forecast is only recalculated.

Current forecast: the Forecast PLAN calculated today. Forecast at planning: the state frozen at the planning (basis of the distribution per product). The difference shows how the forecast has changed since.
80 % interval around the Forecast PLAN, measured from the scatter of the last sprints; it widens with the distance to the last result. With fewer than 5 sprints with velocity only a rough hint.
Finished tickets plus the parts of open tickets completed in the sprint (team practice).
Recommended planning amount: norm. velocity trend / reference capacity × capacity, rounded down. Never negative.
Reserved share of the Forecast PLAN for plannable topics (default 80 %); the rest is called "small items". It is a split of the forecast, not another value: plannable + small items = Forecast PLAN.

Three optional areas that can be switched on independently in the settings (off for new teams): product distribution (several products), PO assignment (product owner per product) and production access (only some people may work on certain tickets). Areas that are switched off hide pages, columns and hints; recorded values stay in the files.
Absences entered by the POs in the pre-planning (forecast, not yet confirmed). Not to be confused with the expected absences.
Estimate from the history (average of the last sprints with confirmed absences) for sprints whose absences are unknown. Calculated, not entered by anyone.
Rest of the Forecast PLAN for bugs, support and small things.
Velocity / commitment – how well was the commitment kept?
Available amount / number of products handled. Available = Forecast PLAN (frozen at planning) or only its plannable share (setting).
Σ done − Σ standard over several sprints.
Forecast PLAN − planning total (carry-over + backlog − corrections). Optional cross-check in planning; does not affect any other metric.
capacity_sources: Value is in the sprint file (frozen at the review or entered manually).
Calculated from people, holidays and absences.
Absences still unknown and no history yet: capacity from the people list and calendar (holidays, sprint length), without deduction for absences.
Only for teams without a people list: capacity extrapolated like the normalized velocity.
Absences not yet confirmed: capacity from the people list with the announced absences entered in the PO pre-planning.
Absences unknown: capacity from the people list and calendar, reduced by the average absences of the last sprints with confirmed absences (setting “Absence history”).
